records.issue_text: embed.js concatenates discourseUrl + "embed/best?..." assuming a trailing slash, producing a malformed URL if discourseUrl lacks one
records.rationale: embed.js does `iframe.src = discourseUrl + "embed/best?..."` with no normalization; if discourseUrl lacks a trailing slash the URL is malformed. Plausible real defect, though actual behavior depends on how discourseUrl is set (not shown in diff), so moderate confidence.

records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb applies discourse_expires_in 1.minute unconditionally to both the loading placeholder and real content responses, causing a cached loading page to be served for up to a minute after real content is available
records.rationale: The diff shows `discourse_expires_in 1.minute` placed at the end of EmbedController#best, applying to both the real-content render and the 'loading' render path (when no topic_id exists). A cached loading placeholder served for up to 60s—longer than the page's own 30s JS reload—can delay real content, a real behavioral defect introduced by this diff.

records.issue_text: No test coverage exists for TopicEmbed.import_remote, leaving the Readability-based remote-fetch/parsing logic untested
records.rationale: The diff adds TopicEmbed.import_remote (ruby-readability based remote fetch/parsing) in app/models/topic_embed.rb, but spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb only covers .import (malformed URL, creation, update) and never exercises import_remote; disqus.thor now calls it too. This is a specific, substantive test-coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a defect or style nit.

records.issue_text: The -c/--category option in lib/tasks/disqus.thor was removed outright instead of deprecated, silently breaking existing script invocations that pass --category
records.rationale: The diff removes `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` and the code consuming `options[:category]` from the Disqus thor task. Thor rejects unknown options at invocation time, so existing scripts passing --category/-c will fail with an 'unknown option' error rather than degrading gracefully. This is a real, verifiable breaking behavior introduced by the diff, though impact is limited to a CLI task's existing users.
